# Solercia Design System: complete manual

> Every chapter of the Solercia design-system manual (packages @solercia/ui, @solercia/eslint-config and
> @solercia/chat) followed by the complete @solercia/ui component reference. Generated from
> docs/manual/*.md and README.md by `npm run docs:llms`; do not edit by hand. Short index: llms.txt.

## Chapters

- 00 Introduction: What the Solercia design system is, who it is for and how to read this manual.
- 01 Principles: The seven decisions behind the Solercia design system and what each one means in code.
- 02 Architecture: How @solercia/ui, @solercia/eslint-config and @solercia/chat fit together, the host ports and the FSD layers.
- 03 Getting started: Create an Angular 22 project with @solercia/ui step by step, or adopt the library in an existing project.
- 04 Theming: Brand an application with a ThemeFile, serve one theme per tenant and use the --sol-* tokens.
- 05 Internationalization: The SOL_I18N contract, the bundled English and Colombian Spanish catalogs and engine adapters.
- 06 Components: The 57 public components and directives of @solercia/ui by category, with links to the reference and the live demos.
- 07 Patterns: How to build screens with @solercia/ui - the five screen states, forms, tables, dialogs on mobile, charts and kanban.
- 08 Linting and architecture rules: What @solercia/eslint-config enforces - FSD boundaries, file placement, naming, wrapped engines and token-only styles - and how to declare exceptions.
- 09 Chat: Embed the Solercia AI assistant with @solercia/chat - configuration, components, API contract and theming.
- 10 For AI agents: Rules, prompts and review checklists for AI coding agents that build Angular screens with the Solercia design system.
- 11 Releases and contributing: How the Solercia packages are versioned and published, and how to contribute a change.
- 12 FAQ: Quick answers about adopting, theming, translating and extending the Solercia design system.
- Appendix: component reference (inputs, outputs, slots and examples of every component)

<!-- chapter 00: docs/manual/00-index.md -->

# Solercia Design System

<p align="center"><img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/solercia-solutions/solercia-ui/main/.github/assets/solercia-mark.svg" alt="Solercia" width="48" height="92"></p>

The Solercia design system is the set of packages, contracts and rules that Solercia Solutions uses to
build Angular applications for several organizations from one code base. It answers three questions
for every screen: which component to use, how it looks for the active organization, and where the
code that uses it belongs.

```bash
ng add @solercia/ui
```

That single command installs the component library, applies the default theme, scaffolds a
Feature-Sliced Design (FSD) project structure and turns the architecture rules into lint rules.

## What it is made of

| Package | Role | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@solercia/ui` | Angular 22 component library: 57 standalone components and directives, theme runtime, i18n contract, `ng add` and generators. | [solercia-ui](https://github.com/solercia-solutions/solercia-ui) |
| `@solercia/eslint-config` | ESLint flat config that enforces FSD boundaries, file placement and token-only styling. | [eslint-config](https://github.com/solercia-solutions/eslint-config) |
| `@solercia/chat` | Embeddable AI assistant chat (streamed answers, sources, history) that reads the same tokens. | [solercia-chat](https://github.com/solercia-solutions/solercia-chat) |

## Who it is for

- **Application developers** building screens: start with [Getting started](https://github.com/solercia-solutions/solercia-ui/blob/main/docs/manual/03-getting-started.md),
  then [Patterns](https://github.com/solercia-solutions/solercia-ui/blob/main/docs/manual/07-patterns.md).
- **Architects and reviewers** deciding how a project is organized: read [Principles](https://github.com/solercia-solutions/solercia-ui/blob/main/docs/manual/01-principles.md),
  [Architecture](https://github.com/solercia-solutions/solercia-ui/blob/main/docs/manual/02-architecture.md) and [Linting and architecture rules](https://github.com/solercia-solutions/solercia-ui/blob/main/docs/manual/08-linting-and-architecture-rules.md).
- **Designers and brand owners** defining how an organization looks: read [Theming](https://github.com/solercia-solutions/solercia-ui/blob/main/docs/manual/04-theming.md).
- **AI coding agents** generating code with the library: read [For AI agents](https://github.com/solercia-solutions/solercia-ui/blob/main/docs/manual/10-for-ai-agents.md), or
  load the whole manual at once from [`llms-full.txt`](https://github.com/solercia-solutions/solercia-ui/blob/main/llms-full.txt).

## How to read this manual

Each chapter stands on its own and opens with an example. Chapters explain the reasoning and the
contracts; the exhaustive list of inputs and outputs of every component lives in one place, the
[component reference](https://github.com/solercia-solutions/solercia-ui/blob/main/README.md#component-reference), and every component has a live demo in the
showcase application.

| Chapter | Read it when you need to |

| [02 Architecture](https://github.com/solercia-solutions/solercia-ui/blob/main/docs/manual/02-architecture.md) | See how the packages, ports and layers fit together. |
| [03 Getting started](https://github.com/solercia-solutions/solercia-ui/blob/main/docs/manual/03-getting-started.md) | Create a new project or adopt the library in an existing one. |
| [04 Theming](https://github.com/solercia-solutions/solercia-ui/blob/main/docs/manual/04-theming.md) | Brand an application or support several organizations. |
| [05 Internationalization](https://github.com/solercia-solutions/solercia-ui/blob/main/docs/manual/05-i18n.md) | Translate the components or plug in your i18n engine. |
| [06 Components](https://github.com/solercia-solutions/solercia-ui/blob/main/docs/manual/06-components.md) | Find the right component for a job. |
| [07 Patterns](https://github.com/solercia-solutions/solercia-ui/blob/main/docs/manual/07-patterns.md) | Build screens: states, forms, tables, dialogs, charts, kanban. |
| [08 Linting and architecture rules](https://github.com/solercia-solutions/solercia-ui/blob/main/docs/manual/08-linting-and-architecture-rules.md) | Know what the linter enforces and how to declare an exception. |
| [09 Chat](https://github.com/solercia-solutions/solercia-ui/blob/main/docs/manual/09-chat.md) | Embed the AI assistant chat. |
| [10 For AI agents](https://github.com/solercia-solutions/solercia-ui/blob/main/docs/manual/10-for-ai-agents.md) | Prompt an agent or review its output. |
| [11 Releases and contributing](https://github.com/solercia-solutions/solercia-ui/blob/main/docs/manual/11-releases-and-contributing.md) | Change the library and publish a version. |
| [12 FAQ](https://github.com/solercia-solutions/solercia-ui/blob/main/docs/manual/12-faq.md) | Find quick answers. |

## Where the documentation lives

The Markdown files in `docs/manual/` are the single source. They are published three ways:

- **Website**: the *Guides* section of the showcase, next to the live demos.
- **AI file**: [`llms-full.txt`](https://github.com/solercia-solutions/solercia-ui/blob/main/llms-full.txt) at the repository root, with every chapter and the
  component reference in one plain-text file; [`llms.txt`](https://github.com/solercia-solutions/solercia-ui/blob/main/llms.txt) is the short index.
- **Manual**: a PDF and a Word document generated with `npm run docs:manual`.

Change the Markdown and the three outputs follow.

<!-- chapter 01: docs/manual/01-principles.md -->

# Principles

```ts
// The whole contract between an application and the design system fits in four providers.
providers: [
  provideTheme(),                                                   // tokens on :root
  { provide: THEME_SOURCE, useExisting: AppThemeSource },           // how to load a theme
  { provide: SOL_TENANT_RESOLVER, useExisting: AppTenantResolver }, // who the tenant is
  { provide: SOL_I18N, useExisting: I18nService },                  // how to translate
]
```

Every rule in this manual follows from seven principles. When a situation is not covered, decide by
them.

## 1. Host-agnostic

The library never calls your API, never reads your session and never assumes an i18n engine. It
declares small ports (injection tokens) and the host application implements them. The same build of
`@solercia/ui` runs in a public-sector portal, a SaaS back office or a mobile web app.

In code: no component imports `HttpClient`, a router service or a translation library. Data comes in
through inputs; events go out through outputs.

## 2. Theme by data, not by code

An organization's look is a JSON document, a `ThemeFile`, not a stylesheet or a fork. The library
resolves it into about 95 `--sol-*` CSS custom properties with light and dark modes, logo, favicon and
fonts. Adding a tenant means storing one more document; no build, no deploy.

## 3. Tokens only

Components and application styles use `var(--sol-*)` for color, typography, spacing, radius, shadow
and motion. No hexadecimal colors, no literal font families, no `!important`, no `::ng-deep`. The lint
preset enforces it, so a hardcoded color fails CI instead of slipping through review.

## 4. Accessible by default

Every interactive component is reachable and operable with the keyboard and announced correctly by
screen readers. Dialogs trap and restore focus and close on Escape; icon-only controls require an
`ariaLabel`; touch targets reach 44 px on touch screens; animations respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
Accessibility is part of a component's contract, not an option.

## 5. English by default, any language by contract

Without configuration every visible text is English, from a bundled catalog. A host plugs its own
engine (Transloco, ngx-translate or the bundled one) through the `SOL_I18N` contract, and a Colombian
Spanish catalog ships with the package. An explicit input always wins over a default text.

## 6. Modern Angular only

Standalone components, `ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush`, signal inputs and outputs, and no zone.js:
the library and its showcase run with `provideZonelessChangeDetection()`. There are no NgModules to
import and no legacy compatibility layers.

## 7. Architecture as code

Applications are organized with Feature-Sliced Design: `app`, `pages`, `widgets`, `features`,
`entities`, `shared`. A layer imports only from layers below it, and each slice exposes a public
`index.ts`. These rules are not a wiki page: `ng add` scaffolds the structure and
`@solercia/eslint-config` checks it on every commit.

## What the principles rule out

| Temptation | Why it is ruled out | Do this instead |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Copy a component and tweak its CSS | Breaks theming and duplicates fixes. | Use inputs, or ask for a new variant. |
| Import Chart.js directly | Charts would ignore the theme and dark mode. | Use `<sol-chart>`. |
| Write `color: #1e293b` | One tenant's color becomes everyone's. | Use `var(--sol-color-text-primary)`. |
| Hardcode Spanish labels | Other organizations cannot translate them. | Use an i18n key or an input. |
| Fetch data inside a shared component | Couples the design system to one API. | Fetch in a feature; pass data down. |

<!-- chapter 02: docs/manual/02-architecture.md -->

# Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Host["Host Angular application"]
    direction TB
    Resolver["AppTenantResolver<br/>who is the tenant"]
    Source["AppThemeSource<br/>how to load its theme"]
    I18n["I18nService<br/>how to translate"]
    Screens["pages / widgets / features"]
  end
  subgraph UI["@solercia/ui"]
    direction TB
    Theme["ThemeService<br/>--sol-* tokens on :root"]
    Comp["sol-* components"]
    Ports["THEME_SOURCE · SOL_TENANT_RESOLVER · SOL_I18N"]
  end
  Lint["@solercia/eslint-config<br/>checks layers and styles"]
  Chat["@solercia/chat<br/>reads the same tokens"]
  Resolver --> Ports
  Source --> Ports
  I18n --> Ports
  Ports --> Theme
  Theme --> Comp
  Screens --> Comp
  Screens --> Chat
  Lint -. lints .-> Screens
```

The design system has three packages. The host application implements a few ports; the library does
everything else.

## The three packages

| Package | Version line | Depends on | Ships |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@solercia/ui` | 0.8 | `@angular/core`, `@angular/common`, `@angular/forms` 22; optional `@angular/cdk`, `chart.js`, `@dagrejs/dagre` | Components, theme runtime, i18n contract and catalogs, `ng add`, generators, secondary entry points `@solercia/ui/theme-studio` and `@solercia/ui/login-appearance` |
| `@solercia/eslint-config` | 0.2 | `eslint` 10, `typescript-eslint` 8, optional `@eslint/css` | FSD boundary, file placement, naming and token-styling rules |
| `@solercia/chat` | 0.4 | `@angular/core`, `@angular/common` 22.1 | `<sol-chat>`, `<sol-chat-flotante>`, `provideSolerciaChat()` |

`@solercia/ui` is the only required package. `ng add @solercia/ui` installs the lint preset for you;
the chat is added only by applications that embed an assistant.

## Ports: what the host provides

The library owns the mechanism; the host owns the policy. Each port is an Angular `InjectionToken`
exported from `@solercia/ui`.

| Port | Question it answers | Contract | Without it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `THEME_SOURCE` | How do I load a tenant's theme? | `loadTheme(tenantId): Promise<ThemeFile \| null>` | No tenant theme loads; the default applies. |
| `SOL_TENANT_RESOLVER` | Who is the active tenant? | `activeTenantId(): number \| null` | Single-theme mode. |
| `SOL_DEFAULT_THEME` | What applies when there is no tenant theme? | `ThemeFile` | The bundled «Vértice» theme. |
| `SOL_I18N` | How do I translate a key? | `activeLang`, `translate`, `t`, `tMany` | English from the bundled catalog. |
| `SOL_CHART_ENGINE` | Which chart engine renders `sol-chart`? | `SolChartEngineFactory` | Chart.js, loaded on the first chart. |
| `SOL_CALENDAR_COLOR` | How are calendar events colored? | `resolve(event, isDark)` | Derived from `event.color` and tokens. |

Only `provideTheme()` is required. Everything else is optional and has a working default.

## Degradation levels

The theme runtime never leaves the application unstyled. It falls back one level at a time:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A["Tenant active?"] -->|yes| B["THEME_SOURCE.loadTheme(id)"]
  A -->|no| D
  B -->|valid ThemeFile| C["Level 1: tenant theme"]
  B -->|null, error or invalid| D["Level 2: SOL_DEFAULT_THEME (Vértice)"]
  D -->|default set to null| E["Level 3: static :root block in styles.css"]
```

| Level | Source | Requires the host? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Tenant theme | `THEME_SOURCE.loadTheme(tenantId)` | Yes: resolver and source. |
| 2. Default theme | `SOL_DEFAULT_THEME`, bundled «Vértice» | No. |
| 3. Inline CSS | A `:root { --sol-*: … }` block in the host's `styles.css` | Host-owned safety net. |

A failed request, a 404 or an invalid document degrades silently from level 1 to level 2 with a
console warning. See [Theming](https://github.com/solercia-solutions/solercia-ui/blob/main/docs/manual/04-theming.md) for the details.

## Application layers (Feature-Sliced Design)

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  app["app<br/>bootstrap, routes, providers"] --> pages["pages<br/>one route each"]
  pages --> widgets["widgets<br/>composite blocks"]
  widgets --> features["features<br/>user actions"]
  features --> entities["entities<br/>business models and APIs"]
  entities --> shared["shared<br/>ui, api, i18n, tokens, lib"]
```

A layer imports only from the layers below it. Inside a layer, code is grouped in slices
(`features/login`, `entities/project`) and segments (`ui`, `model`, `api`, `lib`, `config`). Other
slices import a slice only through its `index.ts`.

| Layer | Holds | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `app` | Bootstrap, root routes, providers | `app.config.ts` with `provideTheme()` |
| `pages` | One routed screen, composition only | `pages/projects/ui/projects-page.component.ts` |
| `widgets` | Self-contained blocks reused across pages | A dashboard summary panel |
| `features` | One user action with its state | `features/invite-member` |
| `entities` | Business models and their API clients | `entities/project/model`, `entities/project/api` |
| `shared` | Code with no business knowledge | Theme and i18n adapters in `shared/tokens`, `shared/i18n` |

`@solercia/ui` components play the role of `shared/ui` for every application: presentational, driven by
inputs, unaware of stores and APIs. Applications add their own `shared/ui` components only when the
library has no equivalent, and those follow the same rules.

## Inside `@solercia/ui`

| Path | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `src/lib/ui/` | One folder per component family (`sol-*`) |
| `src/lib/tokens/` | `ThemeService`, theme ports, the bundled default theme |
| `src/lib/i18n/` | The `SolI18n` contract, `createSolI18n()`, bundled catalogs |
| `src/public-api.ts` | Everything consumers can import |
| `schematics/` | `ng add` and the `page`, `feature`, `entity` and `widget` generators |
| `theme-studio/`, `login-appearance/` | Secondary entry points |

Import every symbol from `@solercia/ui` (or a secondary entry point); deep imports into `lib/` are not
part of the public API.

---

<!-- chapter 03: docs/manual/03-getting-started.md -->

# Getting started

```bash
npx -y @angular/cli@22 new acme-portal --style=css --ssr=false
cd acme-portal
npx ng add @solercia/ui
npx ng serve
```

Four commands give you a zoneless Angular 22 application with the default theme applied, an FSD
project structure, path aliases, theme and i18n adapters, the lint preset and commit hooks.

## Requirements

| Tool | Version |
| --- | --- |
| Node.js | 22.14 or later (24 recommended) |
| Angular | 22 |
| npm | 11 recommended |

## A. New project

### Step 1. Create the application

```bash
npx -y @angular/cli@22 new acme-portal --style=css --ssr=false
```

Angular 22 creates a zoneless application (`provideZonelessChangeDetection()`); `@solercia/ui` needs no
zone.js.

### Step 2. Add the design system

```bash
cd acme-portal
npx ng add @solercia/ui
```

`ng add` (options `--project`, `--skip-install`) does the following:

1. Creates the FSD layer stubs `src/{pages,widgets,features,entities}/index.ts`.
2. Scaffolds `src/shared/tokens/` with `AppThemeSource` and `AppTenantResolver` (both return `null`).
3. Scaffolds `src/shared/i18n/i18n.service.ts`, an `I18nService` that implements `SolI18n`.
4. Adds the path aliases `@app/*`, `@pages/*`, `@widgets/*`, `@features/*`, `@entities/*`, `@shared/*`.
5. Appends the tokens base snippet to `src/styles.css` (page background, text color, font).
6. Adds `provideTheme()` to `app.config.ts`.
7. Creates `eslint.config.js` extending `@solercia/eslint-config`, unless one exists.
8. Sets up Husky, lint-staged and commitlint.
9. Installs the dev dependencies (unless `--skip-install`).

It does not register `THEME_SOURCE` or `SOL_I18N`; the scaffolded adapters explain how when you need
them.

### Step 3. Build a first screen

Generate a page with the library's generator and use components in its `imports`:

```bash
npx ng generate @solercia/ui:page projects
```

```ts
import { ChangeDetectionStrategy, Component, signal } from '@angular/core';
import {
  SolButtonComponent,
  SolCardComponent,
  SolEmptyStateComponent,
  SolPageHeaderComponent,
} from '@solercia/ui';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-projects-page',
  changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush,
  imports: [SolPageHeaderComponent, SolCardComponent, SolButtonComponent, SolEmptyStateComponent],
  template: `
    <sol-page-header title="Projects" subtitle="Everything your team is working on">
      <sol-button (clicked)="create()">New project</sol-button>
    </sol-page-header>
    <sol-card>
      @if (projects().length === 0) {
        <sol-empty-state icon="folder-open" titleKey="pages.projects.empty.title">
          <sol-button variant="secondary" (clicked)="create()">Create the first project</sol-button>
        </sol-empty-state>
      } @else {
        @for (project of projects(); track project) {
          <p>{{ project }}</p>
        }
      }
    </sol-card>
  `,
})
export class ProjectsPageComponent {
  readonly projects = signal<string[]>([]);

  create(): void {
    this.projects.update((list) => [...list, `Project ${list.length + 1}`]);
  }
}
```

The other generators follow the same layers:

| Command | Creates |
| --- | --- |
| `ng generate @solercia/ui:page <name>` | `pages/<name>/` with `index.ts`, `<name>.routes.ts` and `ui/<name>-page.component.ts` |
| `ng generate @solercia/ui:widget <name>` | `widgets/<name>/` with `index.ts` and a standalone `OnPush` component |
| `ng generate @solercia/ui:feature <name>` | `features/<name>/` with `index.ts` and a component using signal inputs and outputs |
| `ng generate @solercia/ui:entity <name>` | `entities/<name>/` with `model/` and `api/` |

### Step 4. Add a light and dark toggle

```ts
import { ChangeDetectionStrategy, Component, inject } from '@angular/core';
import { SolIconButtonComponent, ThemeService } from '@solercia/ui';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-theme-toggle',
  changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush,
  imports: [SolIconButtonComponent],
  template: `
    <sol-icon-button
      variant="ghost"
      [icon]="theme.isDark() ? 'sun' : 'moon'"
      [ariaLabel]="theme.isDark() ? 'Switch to light mode' : 'Switch to dark mode'"
      (clicked)="theme.toggleMode()"
    />
  `,
})
export class ThemeToggleComponent {
  protected readonly theme = inject(ThemeService);
}
```

The user's choice persists in `localStorage` and is independent of the tenant theme.

### Step 5. Check the rules

```bash
npx eslint .
```

A clean run is part of the definition of done. See
[Linting and architecture rules](https://github.com/solercia-solutions/solercia-ui/blob/main/docs/manual/08-linting-and-architecture-rules.md).

## B. Existing project

Adopt the library incrementally; nothing forces you to migrate every screen at once.

### Step 1. Install

```bash
npm install @solercia/ui @angular/cdk chart.js @dagrejs/dagre
```

`@angular/cdk` is needed by the kanban components, `chart.js` by `sol-chart` and `@dagrejs/dagre` by the
flow canvas auto-layout. Install only what you use; `ng add @solercia/ui` also works on an existing
project if you want the scaffolding.

### Step 2. Register the theme runtime

```ts
import { ApplicationConfig, provideZonelessChangeDetection } from '@angular/core';
import { provideRouter } from '@angular/router';
import { provideTheme } from '@solercia/ui';

export const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
  providers: [provideZonelessChangeDetection(), provideRouter([]), provideTheme()],
};
```

### Step 3. Apply the tokens to the page

```css
/* src/styles.css */
body {
  background: var(--sol-bg-page);
  color: var(--sol-color-text-primary);
  font-family: var(--sol-font-family);
}
```

### Step 4. Use components in new screens first

Import components into the standalone `imports` of the screen you are building. Replace hand-written
buttons, tables, dialogs and date pickers as you touch each screen.

### Step 5. Connect your tenant, theme and language (optional)

```ts
import { ApplicationConfig } from '@angular/core';
import { SOL_I18N, SOL_TENANT_RESOLVER, THEME_SOURCE, provideTheme } from '@solercia/ui';
import { AppTenantResolver, AppThemeSource } from '@shared/tokens';
import { I18nService } from '@shared/i18n';

export const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
  providers: [
    provideTheme(),
    { provide: THEME_SOURCE, useExisting: AppThemeSource },
    { provide: SOL_TENANT_RESOLVER, useExisting: AppTenantResolver },
    { provide: SOL_I18N, useExisting: I18nService },
  ],
};
```

[Theming](https://github.com/solercia-solutions/solercia-ui/blob/main/docs/manual/04-theming.md) shows how to implement `AppThemeSource` and `AppTenantResolver`;
[Internationalization](https://github.com/solercia-solutions/solercia-ui/blob/main/docs/manual/05-i18n.md) shows the i18n adapter.

### Step 6. Add the lint preset

```bash
npm install --save-dev @solercia/eslint-config eslint typescript-eslint @eslint/css
```

```js
// eslint.config.js
import solerciaConfig from '@solercia/eslint-config';

export default [
  { ignores: ['.angular/', 'dist/', 'coverage/', 'node_modules/'] },
  ...solerciaConfig,
];
```

In a large legacy code base, start with the style rules on new folders and widen the scope as screens
move into the FSD layers.

## Verification checklist

- [ ] The application renders on the «Vértice» theme with no backend running.
- [ ] The light and dark toggle switches every component and persists after a reload.
- [ ] `npx eslint .` passes.
- [ ] A screen at 390 px wide has no horizontal scroll.
- [ ] Keyboard only: every action is reachable with Tab and Enter or Space.

---

<!-- chapter 04: docs/manual/04-theming.md -->

# Theming

```ts
import { Injectable, signal } from '@angular/core';
import type { SolTenantResolver, ThemeFile, ThemeSource } from '@solercia/ui';

/** WHO: the active organization, null before sign-in. */
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class AppTenantResolver implements SolTenantResolver {
  readonly tenantId = signal<number | null>(null);
  activeTenantId(): number | null {
    return this.tenantId();
  }
}

/** HOW: load that organization's theme. Return null to keep the default. */
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class AppThemeSource implements ThemeSource {
  async loadTheme(tenantId: number | string): Promise<ThemeFile | null> {
    const response = await fetch(`/api/tenants/${tenantId}/theme`);
    return response.ok ? ((await response.json()) as ThemeFile) : null;
  }
}
```

Register both with `useExisting` (see [Getting started](https://github.com/solercia-solutions/solercia-ui/blob/main/docs/manual/03-getting-started.md#step-5-connect-your-tenant-theme-and-language-optional))
and every component re-skins when `tenantId` changes, without a reload.

## How it works

`ThemeService` (`providedIn: 'root'`, started by `provideTheme()`) is the only consumer of the theme
ports. It:

- reads `SOL_TENANT_RESOLVER.activeTenantId()` inside an effect and asks `THEME_SOURCE` for the theme;
- discards stale responses for a tenant that is no longer active;
- validates the document with `isRenderableTheme()` and keeps the previous or default theme when it
  is not renderable;
- writes the resolved `--sol-*` properties on `document.documentElement`;
- manages light and dark mode as a user preference stored in `localStorage` (`sol-dark-mode`);
- derives the logo, brand name, favicon and one sanitized Google Fonts link.

| Member | Kind | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `activeTheme()` | `Signal<ThemeFile \| null>` | The effective theme. |
| `isDark()` | `Signal<boolean>` | Current mode. |
| `logo()` | `Signal<ThemeLogo \| null>` | Sanitized logo for the active mode. |
| `brandName()` | `Signal<string \| null>` | Logo alternative text or tenant slug. |
| `toggleMode()` / `setDarkMode(dark)` | method | Change the mode and persist it. |
| `setTenantTheme(theme)` | method | Apply a `ThemeFile` directly, bypassing `THEME_SOURCE` (validated). |
| `refresh()` | method | Reload the active tenant's theme, for example after saving it. |

The library never fetches a theme by itself: where the document comes from (an API, a file, a
database `jsonb` column) is the host's decision.

## The `ThemeFile`

A theme is a three-level token document aligned with the W3C Design Tokens format:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  P["primitives<br/>palette, font scale, radius, space"] --> S["modes.light / modes.dark<br/>semantic: primary, text, surface, border"]
  S --> C["component<br/>card, input, button, sidebar, chart, motion"]
  C --> V["--sol-* custom properties"]
```

```jsonc
{
  "meta": { "tenant": "acme", "logo": { "url": "/assets/acme.svg", "altText": "ACME", "width": 120 } },
  "primitives": { "color": { "brand": { "600": "#6D28D9" } } /* font, radius, space, size, z, borderWidth */ },
  "modes": {
    "light": { "semantic": { "color": { "primary": "{color.brand.600}" } /* … */ }, "component": { /* … */ } },
    "dark":  { "semantic": { "color": { "primary": "{color.brand.600}" } /* … */ }, "component": { /* … */ } }
  }
}
```

- Values can reference primitives with `{path}`, as a whole value or inside a shorthand
  (`"1px solid {color.ink.200}"`).
- Both `modes.light` and `modes.dark` are required.
- Blocks introduced after the first version (card, input, button, sidebar, chart, motion, overlay,
  table, calendar) are optional; a missing block emits its baseline default, so older themes keep
  working.
- Background images accept gradients or `none` only; logos and favicons accept `http`, `https` or
  relative URLs; fonts are Google Fonts built from `family` and `weights`, never from a raw URL.

The full contract, with every field and a minimal complete example, is in
[`THEMING.md`](https://github.com/solercia-solutions/solercia-ui/blob/main/projects/solercia/ui/docs/THEMING.md). The bundled reference theme «Vértice», with
every optional block filled in, is `SOL_BUNDLED_DEFAULT_THEME`.

## The tokens

Use these groups in your own styles. The authoritative list, with the contract path and default of
each variable, is `EMIT_TABLE`.

| Group | Examples |
| --- | --- |
| Color | `--sol-color-primary`, `--sol-color-primary-contrast`, `--sol-color-secondary`, `--sol-color-accent`, `--sol-color-success`, `--sol-color-warning`, `--sol-color-danger`, `--sol-color-info` |
| Text | `--sol-color-text-primary`, `--sol-color-text-secondary`, `--sol-color-text-muted` |
| Surfaces | `--sol-bg-page`, `--sol-bg-surface`, `--sol-bg-sunken`, `--sol-bg-overlay`, `--sol-bg-page-texture` |
| Typography | `--sol-font-family`, `--sol-font-family-mono`, `--sol-font-display`, `--sol-font-numeric`, `--sol-font-size-sm`, `--sol-font-size-base`, `--sol-font-size-lg`, `--sol-font-size-xl`, `--sol-font-weight-bold`, `--sol-line-height` |
| Spacing | `--sol-space-xs`, `--sol-space-sm`, `--sol-space-md`, `--sol-space-lg`, `--sol-space-xl` |
| Shape | `--sol-border-radius-sm`, `--sol-border-radius-md`, `--sol-border-radius-lg`, `--sol-border-radius-full`, `--sol-border-width-default`, `--sol-border-color-default` |
| Elevation | `--sol-shadow-sm`, `--sol-shadow-md`, `--sol-shadow-lg`, `--sol-shadow-card` |
| Sizes | `--sol-size-input-height`, `--sol-size-button-height`, `--sol-size-control-touch`, `--sol-size-header-height`, `--sol-size-sidebar-width` |
| Layers | `--sol-z-dropdown`, `--sol-z-modal`, `--sol-z-tooltip` |
| Motion | `--sol-dur-fast`, `--sol-dur-base`, `--sol-dur-slow`, `--sol-ease`, `--sol-ease-entrance` |
| Components | `--sol-card-*`, `--sol-input-*`, `--sol-button-*`, `--sol-sidebar-*`, `--sol-header-*`, `--sol-chart-1` to `--sol-chart-6` |

```css
.summary {
  padding: var(--sol-space-lg);
  border: var(--sol-border-width-default) solid var(--sol-border-color-default);
  border-radius: var(--sol-border-radius-lg);
  background: var(--sol-bg-surface);
  color: var(--sol-color-text-primary);
}
.summary__value {
  font-family: var(--sol-font-numeric);
  color: var(--sol-color-primary);
}
```

## Your own default theme

Provide your brand theme as the default. It becomes level 2 and the look before sign-in:

```ts
import { SOL_DEFAULT_THEME, type ThemeFile } from '@solercia/ui';
import brandTheme from './brand.theme.json';

export const brandThemeProvider = { provide: SOL_DEFAULT_THEME, useValue: brandTheme as ThemeFile };
```

## Level 3: the static safety net

Add a `:root { --sol-*: … }` block to `styles.css` with literal values. `ThemeService` removes its inline
properties when it has no applicable theme, so this block governs only as a last resort. The lint
preset allows literals where a custom property is defined.

## Editing themes: Theme Studio

`@solercia/ui/theme-studio` provides `<sol-theme-studio>`, a complete theme editor with live preview,
backed by a host store contract (`THEME_STUDIO_STORE`). Use it to let each organization edit its own
theme and call `ThemeService.refresh()` after saving. See
[`THEME-STUDIO.md`](https://github.com/solercia-solutions/solercia-ui/blob/main/projects/solercia/ui/docs/THEME-STUDIO.md).

## Themed sign-in

A theme can carry a `meta.login` block (photos, motion, per-mode composition). The entry point
`@solercia/ui/login-appearance` paints it with `<sol-login-frame>` and ships no authentication logic:
the host projects its own form. See the [README section](https://github.com/solercia-solutions/solercia-ui/blob/main/README.md#themed-sign-in-solerciauilogin-appearance).

## Checklist

- [ ] With no tenant, the application renders on the default theme.
- [ ] Switching tenant re-skins the UI live; a failing theme request keeps the default.
- [ ] Dark mode is independent of the tenant and persists across reloads.
- [ ] No literal color, font or `!important` in component styles.

---

<!-- chapter 05: docs/manual/05-i18n.md -->

# Internationalization

```ts
import { SOL_I18N, createSolI18n } from '@solercia/ui';

// Colombian Spanish for every component, no i18n engine needed.
export const spanishProvider = { provide: SOL_I18N, useFactory: () => createSolI18n({ lang: 'es-CO' }) };
```

Components never import Transloco, ngx-translate or `@angular/localize`. They depend on one small
contract, `SolI18n`, that the host binds to `SOL_I18N`. The pattern mirrors Angular Material's `*Intl`
services.

## The contract

```ts
import type { Signal } from '@angular/core';

interface SolI18n {
  readonly activeLang: Signal<string>;
  translate(key: string, params?: Record<string, unknown>): string; // missing key: returns the key
  t(key: string, params?: Record<string, unknown>): Signal<string>; // recomputes on language change
  tMany(keys: string[]): Signal<string[]>;
}
```

| Member | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `activeLang` | Reacting to language changes, for example a language selector. |
| `translate(key, params?)` | One-off lookups in imperative code. |
| `t(key, params?)` | Template bindings; call it in an injection context. |
| `tMany(keys)` | Ordered lists such as stepper labels. |

## Three ways to provide it

| Situation | Provider |
| --- | --- |
| English is enough | Nothing. `SOL_I18N` defaults to `createSolI18n()`, English from the bundled catalog. |
| Spanish or another fixed language, no engine | `{ provide: SOL_I18N, useFactory: () => createSolI18n({ lang: 'es-CO' }) }` |
| The application already uses an engine | A facade with the four members, bound with `useExisting`. |

`createSolI18n(options?)` returns a `SolCatalogI18n` with `setLang(lang)`. Its options are `lang`
(default `'en'`) and `catalogs` (default `{ en: SOL_I18N_EN, 'es-CO': SOL_I18N_ES_CO }`):

```ts
import { SOL_I18N_EN, createSolI18n, type SolI18nCatalog } from '@solercia/ui';

declare const frenchCatalog: SolI18nCatalog;

const i18n = createSolI18n({ lang: 'fr', catalogs: { en: SOL_I18N_EN, fr: frenchCatalog } });
i18n.setLang('en');
```

### Adapter for Transloco

```ts
import { Injectable, Signal, inject } from '@angular/core';
import { TranslocoService, translateSignal } from '@jsverse/transloco';

@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class I18nService {
  private readonly transloco = inject(TranslocoService);
  readonly activeLang: Signal<string> = this.transloco.activeLang;

  translate(key: string, params?: Record<string, unknown>): string {
    return this.transloco.translate(key, params);
  }
  t(key: string, params?: Record<string, unknown>): Signal<string> {
    return translateSignal(key, params);
  }
  tMany(keys: string[]): Signal<string[]> {
    return translateSignal(keys);
  }
}

// app.config.ts: { provide: SOL_I18N, useExisting: I18nService }
```

The same shape works for ngx-translate or any other engine: bridge its language-change stream into a
signal with `toSignal` so `activeLang`, `t` and `tMany` recompute. More examples are in
[`I18N.md`](https://github.com/solercia-solutions/solercia-ui/blob/main/projects/solercia/ui/docs/I18N.md).

## Bundled catalogs and fallback

Every visible default text in the library goes through a `shared.*` key. Both catalogs ship with the
package:

| Catalog | Constant | File |
| --- | --- | --- |
| English | `SOL_I18N_EN` | `@solercia/ui/i18n/en.json` |
| Colombian Spanish | `SOL_I18N_ES_CO` | `@solercia/ui/i18n/es-CO.json` |

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["Explicit input<br/>confirmLabel='Delete'"] -->|set| R["Rendered text"]
  A -->|not set| B["Host engine<br/>translate('shared.confirmDialog.confirm')"]
  B -->|translated| R
  B -->|returns the key unchanged| C["Bundled catalog of the active language<br/>es* → es-CO, else en"]
  C --> R
```

- An explicit input (`searchPlaceholder`, `actionsLabel`, `confirmLabel`, `label`) always wins.
- When the host engine does not know a `shared.*` key, the component falls back to the bundled
  catalog of the active language, so a host catalog does not need every library key and keys added in
  later versions keep the host language.
- With Transloco or ngx-translate you can also merge `@solercia/ui/i18n/es-CO.json` into your `es-CO`
  translations.

## Inputs that take keys

Inputs whose name ends in `Key` receive an i18n key, not a text: `titleKey` and `descriptionKey` on
`sol-empty-state`, `ariaLabelKey` on `sol-chart` and `sol-number-input`, `labelKey` on timeline nodes.

```html
<sol-empty-state icon="folder-open" titleKey="pages.projects.empty.title" descriptionKey="pages.projects.empty.description" />
```

## Rules for application code

- Put your own texts in your catalog under your own namespaces (`pages.*`, `features.*`); keep
  `shared.*` for the library.
- Never hard-code a visible text in a shared component; take it as an input or a key.
- Tests that assert texts should use the catalogs, not literals typed in the spec.
- `createIdentitySolI18n()` returns keys unchanged and is meant for tests.

<!-- chapter 06: docs/manual/06-components.md -->

# Components

```ts
import { SolButtonComponent, SolDataTableComponent, SolModalComponent } from '@solercia/ui';

// Every component is standalone: add it to the `imports` of the component that uses it.
export const projectScreenImports = [SolButtonComponent, SolDataTableComponent, SolModalComponent];
```

`@solercia/ui` has 57 public components and directives. This chapter helps you choose one; the
[component reference](https://github.com/solercia-solutions/solercia-ui/blob/main/README.md#component-reference) lists every input, output and slot, and the
showcase demoes each component live, in light and dark mode, down to 390 px.

Conventions used across the library:

- Selectors start with `sol-`; directives with `sol` (`[solReveal]`, `*solWizardStep`, `*solTreeNodeDef`).
- Class names are `Sol<Name>Component` or `Sol<Name>Directive`.
- Form controls implement `ControlValueAccessor`, so `[(ngModel)]` and `formControlName` work.
- Outputs are past-tense or `*Change` events: `clicked`, `closed`, `valueChange`, `itemMoved`.
- Inputs ending in `Key` take an i18n key; icon-only controls require `ariaLabel`.

| Selector | Use it for | Demo |

| `sol-button` | Text button with `primary`, `secondary`, `danger` and `ghost` variants and a loading state. | [Buttons](https://solercia-solutions.github.io/solercia-ui/buttons) |
| `sol-icon-button` | Icon-only action; `ariaLabel` is required. | [Buttons](https://solercia-solutions.github.io/solercia-ui/buttons) |
| `sol-icon` | Inline SVG from a registry of about 140 names. | [Icons](https://solercia-solutions.github.io/solercia-ui/icons) |

## Secondary entry points

| Entry point | Provides |
| --- | --- |
| `@solercia/ui/theme-studio` | `<sol-theme-studio>` theme editor and its store contract. |
| `@solercia/ui/login-appearance` | `<sol-login-frame>` and the pieces of a themed sign-in screen. |

## Choosing between similar components

| If you need | Use | Not |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A yes or no that applies immediately | `sol-toggle` | `sol-checkbox` |
| A yes or no submitted with a form, or a list of options | `sol-checkbox` | `sol-toggle` |
| Two to five mutually exclusive views | `sol-view-toggle` | `sol-tabs` |
| Sections of one page with their own content | `sol-tabs` | `sol-view-toggle` |
| A short decision about a destructive action | `sol-confirm-dialog` | `sol-modal` |
| A form or task in context | `sol-drawer` | `sol-modal` on phones |
| A placeholder that keeps the layout while loading | `sol-skeleton` | `sol-spinner` |
| A busy indicator inside a button or small area | `sol-spinner` or `sol-button [loading]` | `sol-skeleton` |

<!-- chapter 07: docs/manual/07-patterns.md -->

# Patterns

```html
@switch (state()) {
  @case ('loading') { <sol-skeleton variant="row" count="5" /> }
  @case ('error') {
    <sol-empty-state icon="exclamation-triangle" titleKey="pages.projects.error.title">
      <sol-button variant="secondary" (clicked)="reload()">Try again</sol-button>
    </sol-empty-state>
  }
  @case ('empty') {
    <sol-empty-state icon="folder-open" titleKey="pages.projects.empty.title">
      <sol-button (clicked)="create()">Create project</sol-button>
    </sol-empty-state>
  }
  @case ('no-results') { <sol-empty-state icon="funnel" titleKey="pages.projects.noResults.title" /> }
  @default { <sol-data-table [data]="visible()" [columns]="columns" /> }
}
```

A pattern is a proven way to combine components for a recurring screen. Follow these before
designing something new.

## The five screen states

Every screen that shows data has five states. Design and test all of them.

| State | Meaning | Component | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Loading | The request is in flight. | `sol-skeleton` for content areas, `sol-spinner` for small areas, `[loading]` on buttons | Keep the layout: the skeleton has the shape of the content. |
| Empty | The request succeeded and there is nothing yet. | `sol-empty-state` with a call to action | Tell the user how to create the first item. |
| No results | There is data, but the filters hide all of it. | `sol-empty-state` with a reset action | Never show the "empty" message: offer to clear the filters. |
| Error | The request failed. | `sol-empty-state` with a retry action | Never confuse "no data" with "the request failed". |
| Success | Data is shown, or an action completed. | The content; a confirmation message | Confirm actions that changed data. |

Derive the state from signals instead of juggling flags:

```ts
import { ChangeDetectionStrategy, Component, computed, signal } from '@angular/core';
import {
  SolButtonComponent,
  SolDataTableComponent,
  SolEmptyStateComponent,
  SolSkeletonComponent,
  type DataTableColumn,
  type SolDataTableRow,
} from '@solercia/ui';

type ScreenState = 'loading' | 'error' | 'empty' | 'no-results' | 'ready';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-projects-list',
  changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush,
  imports: [SolButtonComponent, SolDataTableComponent, SolEmptyStateComponent, SolSkeletonComponent],
  template: `
    @switch (state()) {
      @case ('loading') { <sol-skeleton variant="row" count="5" /> }
      @case ('error') {
        <sol-empty-state icon="exclamation-triangle" titleKey="pages.projects.error.title">
          <sol-button variant="secondary" (clicked)="reload()">Try again</sol-button>
        </sol-empty-state>
      }
      @case ('empty') { <sol-empty-state icon="folder-open" titleKey="pages.projects.empty.title" /> }
      @case ('no-results') {
        <sol-empty-state icon="funnel" titleKey="pages.projects.noResults.title">
          <sol-button variant="ghost" (clicked)="query.set('')">Clear filters</sol-button>
        </sol-empty-state>
      }
      @default { <sol-data-table [data]="visible()" [columns]="columns" /> }
    }
  `,
})
export class ProjectsListComponent {
  readonly loading = signal(true);
  readonly failed = signal(false);
  readonly rows = signal<SolDataTableRow[]>([]);
  readonly query = signal('');
  readonly columns: DataTableColumn[] = [{ key: 'name', label: 'Name', sortable: true }];

  readonly visible = computed(() =>
    this.rows().filter((row) => String(row['name']).toLowerCase().includes(this.query().toLowerCase())),
  );
  readonly state = computed<ScreenState>(() => {
    if (this.loading()) return 'loading';
    if (this.failed()) return 'error';
    if (this.rows().length === 0) return 'empty';
    return this.visible().length === 0 ? 'no-results' : 'ready';
  });

  reload(): void {
    this.failed.set(false);
    this.loading.set(true);
  }
}
```

For lists, `sol-data-table [loading]` and `sol-notification-panel [loading] [error]` already render
their own loading and empty states.

## Forms

- Use the library controls; they implement `ControlValueAccessor` and work with reactive forms
  (`formControlName`) and `ngModel`.
- Give every control a visible `label`. Use `sol-form-field` to wrap a native or third-party control.
- Show validation messages through the `error` input, after the user leaves the field or submits.
- If the system knows the valid values, offer them (`sol-select`, `sol-date-picker`, `sol-day-picker`)
  instead of free text.
- Preselect the most likely value; do not start a form empty when a sensible default exists.
- Long forms become a `sol-wizard`, one `*solWizardStep` per group of fields.

```html
<form [formGroup]="form" (ngSubmit)="save()">
  <sol-input label="Project name" formControlName="name" [error]="nameError()" />
  <sol-select label="Owner" formControlName="owner" [options]="owners()" />
  <sol-date-picker formControlName="dueDate" />
  <sol-button type="submit" [loading]="saving()">Save</sol-button>
</form>
```

## Tables

- `sol-data-table` handles sorting, per-column filters (`filter: 'text' | 'select'`), global search and
  pagination on the client. For server-side paging, pass the current page and use `sol-pagination`.
- Below `collapseWidth` (767 px by default) rows collapse into cards, so tables work on phones without
  horizontal scrolling.
- Put the primary action of the screen in the `[tableActions]` slot and row actions in the
  `#rowActions` template, or use the built-in `editClicked` and `deleteClicked` outputs.
- A delete action always goes through `sol-confirm-dialog`.

## Dialogs on mobile

| Component | Phone behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `sol-confirm-dialog` | Below 640 px it opens as a bottom sheet with full-width stacked actions and Cancel at the bottom, near the thumb. |
| `sol-drawer` | `variant="sheet"` opens from the bottom; use it for filters and short forms. |
| `sol-select` | Opens as a bottom sheet below `mobileBreakpoint` (640 px). |
| `sol-modal` | Keep modals short on phones; prefer a drawer sheet or a page for long forms. |

All of them are `aria-modal`, trap focus, restore it on close, close on Escape when closeable and lock
the page scroll. On touch screens every action reaches the 44 px touch target
(`--sol-size-control-touch`).

```html
<sol-confirm-dialog
  [open]="confirming()"
  title="Delete this project?"
  message="Its tasks and files are deleted too."
  confirmLabel="Delete"
  (confirm)="remove()"
  (cancel)="confirming.set(false)"
/>
```

## Charts

- Use `sol-chart`; never import Chart.js in application code. The chart reads `--sol-chart-1` to
  `--sol-chart-6`, re-renders on light and dark changes, and Chart.js loads only when the first chart
  is created.
- `ariaLabelKey` is required: describe what the chart shows.
- Show a `sol-skeleton variant="card"` while data loads and a `sol-empty-state` when the series are
  empty.

```html
<sol-chart
  type="bar"
  ariaLabelKey="pages.dashboard.projectsByStatus"
  [data]="{ labels: ['Planned', 'Active', 'Done'], series: [{ label: 'Projects', data: [4, 9, 12] }] }"
/>
```

## Kanban

- Use `sol-kanban-board`; never import `@angular/cdk/drag-drop` in application code. The board
  supports mouse, touch and a keyboard "Move to…" menu.
- Update the columns optimistically and call `rollback()` when persisting fails.

```ts
import type { KanbanItemMoved, SolKanbanBoardComponent } from '@solercia/ui';

interface Task {
  id: string;
  title: string;
}

declare function moveTask(move: KanbanItemMoved<Task>): Promise<void>;

export async function persistMove(move: KanbanItemMoved<Task>, board: SolKanbanBoardComponent<Task>): Promise<void> {
  try {
    await moveTask(move);
  } catch {
    board.rollback();
  }
}
```

## Responsive and accessible by default

- Check every screen at 390 px: no horizontal scroll, no hidden primary action.
- Every action must work with the keyboard; icon-only buttons need `ariaLabel`.
- Animate with `[solReveal]` and the motion tokens only; they respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.

---

<!-- chapter 08: docs/manual/08-linting-and-architecture-rules.md -->

# Linting and architecture rules

```js
// eslint.config.js
import solerciaConfig from '@solercia/eslint-config';

export default [
  { ignores: ['.angular/', 'dist/', 'coverage/', 'node_modules/'] },
  ...solerciaConfig,
];
```

`@solercia/eslint-config` turns the architecture into rules the linter checks on every commit. A file
in the wrong folder, an import across layers or a hardcoded color fails CI instead of slipping
through review. `ng add @solercia/ui` installs and configures it.

## Requirements

| Dependency | Version | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Node.js | 22.14 or later | |
| `eslint` | 10 | Flat config only. |
| `typescript-eslint` | 8 | Syntactic rules; no type information needed. |
| `@eslint/css` | 2, optional | When installed, `.css` files are checked too. |

## What it enforces

| Area | Rule | Enforces |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Layer boundaries | `no-restricted-imports` | `app → pages → widgets → features → entities → shared`. A layer imports only from layers below it; `shared/**` never imports from upper layers or `@app/*`. |
| Public API | `no-restricted-imports` | Slices are consumed through their `index.ts` (`@features/login`), never through deep paths (`@features/login/ui/form`). |
| Smart and dumb UI | `no-restricted-imports` | `shared/ui` holds presentational components only: no imports from `entities/`, `features/`, `*.store` or `*.facade`. |
| Wrapped engines | `no-restricted-imports`, `no-restricted-syntax` | `chart.js` only inside `shared/ui/chart`, `maplibre-gl` only inside `shared/ui/map`, `@angular/cdk` only through the `sol-kanban-*` components. |
| Naming | `@typescript-eslint/naming-convention` | `PascalCase` classes, interfaces and types; `camelCase` variables, functions and parameters. |
| File names | `solercia/filename-case` | Every dot-separated segment is kebab-case: `appointment-form.component.ts`. |
| File placement | `solercia/fsd-placement` | Every `.ts` file under `src/` belongs to a layer and an allowed segment. |
| Theme styles | `solercia/style-tokens` | Inline component `styles` and `style="..."` in inline templates use theme variables. |
| Theme styles (CSS) | `solercia/css-style-tokens` | The same checks on `src/**/*.css`, when `@eslint/css` is installed. |

### File placement

```text
src/
├── main.ts                      allowed outside layers (also test-setup.ts, polyfills.ts, environments/**)
├── app/                         anything goes (bootstrap, routes, providers)
├── pages/<slice>/               index.ts, <slice>.routes.ts, ui/
├── widgets/<slice>/<segment>/
├── features/<slice>/<segment>/  segment ∈ ui | model | api | lib | config | testing
├── entities/<slice>/<segment>/  slice groups are allowed: pages/admin/users/ui/
└── shared/<segment>/            segment ∈ api | config | crud | i18n | lib | model | tenant | tokens | ui
```

### Styles

| Reported | Use instead |
| --- | --- |
| Color literals: `#fff`, `rgb()`, `hsl()`, `oklch()`, named colors | `var(--sol-*)` |
| A literal `font-family` | `var(--sol-font-family)` or the matching theme variable |
| `!important` | A more specific selector or a theme variable |
| `::ng-deep` | A CSS custom property exposed by the child component |

Literals stay allowed where tokens are defined and as fallbacks inside `var()`:

```css
:host {
  --sol-card-bg: #ffffff;                       /* defining a custom property */
  background: var(--sol-bg-surface, #ffffff);   /* fallback inside var() */
}
```

Not covered: external templates (`templateUrl`) and `px` units.

## Options

```js
import { solerciaEslintConfig } from '@solercia/eslint-config';

export default [
  ...solerciaEslintConfig({
    srcDir: 'apps/web/src',            // FSD root, default 'src'
    extraSharedSegments: ['support'],  // project-specific shared/ segments
    allowOutsideLayers: ['main.ts'],   // replaces the default bootstrap allow-list
  }),
];
```

The style rules accept `{ allowImportant?: boolean, allowNgDeep?: boolean }`.

## Declaring exceptions

Exceptions live in the consuming project's `eslint.config.js`, never in the preset, so they stay
visible in code review. Each one carries a comment that explains why.

```js
export default [
  ...solerciaEslintConfig({ extraSharedSegments: ['support'] }),
  // Overrides a third-party theme: !important is intentional here.
  {
    files: ['src/assets/legacy-theme.css'],
    rules: { 'solercia/css-style-tokens': ['error', { allowImportant: true }] },
  },
];
```

For a single line, write the reason next to the directive:

```css
/* eslint-disable-next-line solercia/css-style-tokens -- print stylesheet needs pure black */
```

| Acceptable exception | Not acceptable |
| --- | --- |
| Overriding a third-party stylesheet you do not control | Silencing a rule because a deadline is close |
| A print stylesheet that needs absolute colors | Disabling a layer rule to import a feature from an entity |
| A wrapper around a new engine, declared next to the existing ones | Importing Chart.js in a page |

## Commit hooks

`ng add` also configures Husky: `pre-commit` runs `lint-staged` and `commit-msg` runs commitlint with
the Conventional Commits preset, so broken rules and malformed messages stop before they are
committed.

<!-- chapter 09: docs/manual/09-chat.md -->

# Chat

```ts
import { ApplicationConfig } from '@angular/core';
import { provideSolerciaChat } from '@solercia/chat';

export const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
  providers: [
    provideSolerciaChat({
      apiBase: '/support/api',
      textos: { titulo: 'Help' },
    }),
  ],
};
```

```html
<sol-chat-flotante
  [(abierto)]="chatOpen"
  [lanzador]="true"
  [contexto]="{ ruta: '/contracts/payment-reports', titulo: 'Payment reports' }"
  titulo="Assistant"
/>
```

`@solercia/chat` is an embeddable assistant: answers streamed over Server-Sent Events, the current
screen as optional context, cited sources, conversation history and a floating bubble. It ships the
user interface only; the service that answers is separate and implements the API contract below.

## Why a separate package

- Its only peer dependencies are `@angular/core` and `@angular/common` (22.1), so it can be added to
  applications that do not use `@solercia/ui` yet.
- It reads the same `--sol-*` tokens, so inside a Solercia application it follows the tenant theme and
  dark mode without configuration, and it falls back to its own light and dark palette elsewhere.
- It streams with `fetch` and `ReadableStream`; host `HttpClient` interceptors are not involved. Send
  any header the API needs (XSRF token, authorization) through `cabeceras()`.

> **Naming note.** The public API uses Spanish identifiers (`contexto`, `titulo`, `cabeceras`) because
> the package was born in Spanish-speaking public-sector projects. They are stable API; the English
> meaning is given below.

## Configuration

`provideSolerciaChat(config?)` registers `SOLERCIA_CHAT_CONFIG`. To keep the package out of the initial
bundle, provide the configuration in the component that uses the chat instead.

| Field | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `apiBase` | Base URL of the chat API | `'/api'` |
| `credentials` | `fetch` credentials mode | `'include'` |
| `cabeceras` | Extra request headers, evaluated per request | none |
| `textos` | Override any visible text (`Partial<TextosChat>`) | `TEXTOS_CHAT_POR_DEFECTO`, Spanish |
| `maxCaracteres` | Maximum question length | `1000` |
| `persistir` | Keep the conversation in `sessionStorage` | `true` |
| `claveAlmacen` | Storage key; share it to resume a conversation across screens | `'solercia-chat'` |
| `maxHistorial` | Previous turns sent to the API | `10` |
| `historial` | Enable the saved-conversations list | `false` |

Default texts are Colombian Spanish; pass `textos` to localize.

## Components

| Component | Use it for | Key inputs and outputs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<sol-chat>` | An inline chat in a page or side panel | `contexto` (screen), `titulo` (title), `subtitulo` (subtitle), `sugerencias` (up to 4 suggested questions), `compacto` (dense), `contraido` (collapsed), `historial`; outputs `respuesta` (answer) and `error` |
| `<sol-chat-flotante>` | A floating bubble in the bottom-right corner | `abierto` (open, two-way), `contraido` (minimized, two-way), `lanzador` (launcher button), `conModoCompleto` (full-screen button); outputs `modoCompleto`, `cerrado`, `respuesta`, `error` |

Only one chat is open at a time: while an inline `<sol-chat>` is mounted, the bubble stays hidden. The
context chip can be removed and attached again by the user and travels with the request only while
attached.

## API contract

`POST {apiBase}/chat` with `Accept: text/event-stream`:

```json
{
  "pregunta": "How do I submit a payment report?",
  "historial": [{ "rol": "usuario", "texto": "…" }, { "rol": "asistente", "texto": "…" }],
  "conversacionId": "uuid generated by the browser",
  "contexto": { "ruta": "/contracts/payment-reports", "titulo": "Payment reports" }
}
```

| Server-Sent Event | Data |
| --- | --- |
| `fuentes` | Sources retrieved for the answer |
| `cola` | Queue position: `posicion`, `esperaEstimadaSegundos` |
| `fragmento` | Answer chunk: `texto` |
| `fin` | Final answer: `estado`, `respuesta`, `citas`, `documentos`, `casos` |
| `error` | Error envelope with `status.appDesc` and `status.appCode` |

With `historial: true` the chat also calls `GET`, `PATCH` and `DELETE` on `{apiBase}/conversaciones`.
The full contract, including history payloads, is in the
[`@solercia/chat` README](https://github.com/solercia-solutions/solercia-chat#api-contract).

## Rules

1. Configure once with `provideSolerciaChat`; do not wrap the API in `HttpClient`.
2. Customize through inputs and `textos`; do not fork templates or style internals.
3. A backend built for the chat implements the API contract exactly, including the event names.
4. Markdown in answers is rendered as an Angular node tree, never through `innerHTML`.

<!-- chapter 10: docs/manual/10-for-ai-agents.md -->

# For AI agents

```text
Build the "Projects" page with @solercia/ui.
Read https://raw.githubusercontent.com/solercia-solutions/solercia-ui/main/llms-full.txt first.
Place it in src/pages/projects/ (FSD). Use sol-page-header, sol-data-table and sol-confirm-dialog.
Cover loading, empty, no-results, error and success. Style only with var(--sol-*).
Texts through i18n keys under pages.projects.*. Run npx eslint on the changed files before finishing.
```

This chapter is written for two readers: the AI coding agent that generates code with the design
system, and the person who prompts it and reviews its output.

## What to give an agent

| Source | Content | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`llms.txt`](https://github.com/solercia-solutions/solercia-ui/blob/main/llms.txt) | Short index: setup, providers, components by category, rules | Always; it is small. |
| [`llms-full.txt`](https://github.com/solercia-solutions/solercia-ui/blob/main/llms-full.txt) | This whole manual plus the complete component reference | Screens that use several components, or a new project. |
| `AGENTS.md` of the repository | Repository-specific commands and rules | Changes inside a Solercia repository. |
| The matching showcase page in `projects/showcase/src/app/pages/` | A working example | A component the agent has not used before. |

Both files ship inside the `@solercia/ui` npm package, so an agent can read them from
`node_modules/@solercia/ui/` without network access. `@solercia/eslint-config` and `@solercia/chat`
ship their own `llms.txt`.

## Rules for agents

1. **Reuse before you build.** Look up the component list first; do not hand-roll a button, table,
   modal, date picker or chart that already exists.
2. **Style only with tokens.** `var(--sol-*)` for color, typography, spacing, radius, shadow and
   motion. No literal colors or fonts, no `!important`, no `::ng-deep`.
3. **Respect required inputs.** Every icon-only control has an `ariaLabel`; `sol-chart` has an
   `ariaLabelKey`; `sol-empty-state` has a `titleKey`.
4. **Wrap engines, do not import them.** `<sol-chart>` instead of Chart.js; `sol-kanban-*` instead of
   `@angular/cdk` drag and drop.
5. **Cover every state.** Loading, empty, no results, error and success are part of every screen.
6. **Place files by layer first.** Decide the FSD layer and segment, then write the file. Import slices
   through their `index.ts`.
7. **Modern Angular only.** Standalone, `OnPush`, `input()` and `output()`, signals, built-in control flow
   (`@if`, `@for`, `@switch`). Do not add zone.js or NgModules.
8. **Texts through i18n.** Visible texts come from keys or inputs, never hard-coded in shared components.
9. **Never invent APIs.** If an input, output or symbol is not in the reference, it does not exist. Ask,
   or propose a change to the library instead.
10. **Fix violations at the source.** Do not add `eslint-disable` comments or loosen the config unless the
    user asks; declare a needed exception in `eslint.config.js` with a reason.

## Prompt patterns

**A new screen**

```text
Create the <name> page in src/pages/<name>/ using @solercia/ui.
Data: <entity> from <endpoint or entity slice>. Actions: <list>.
States: loading (skeleton), empty (with create action), no results (clear filters), error (retry).
Phone: must work at 390 px. Keyboard: every action reachable.
```

**A change to an existing screen**

```text
In <file>, replace the hand-written table with sol-data-table. Keep the current columns and
actions. Do not change the API calls. Show the diff and the eslint result.
```

**A theme**

```text
Write a ThemeFile for <organization> with primary <color> and secondary <color>.
Both light and dark modes. Validate it with isRenderableTheme() in a unit test.
```

## Review checklist

Use it on every change an agent proposes.

- [ ] Uses existing `sol-*` components; nothing duplicated.
- [ ] Every symbol and input exists in the reference.
- [ ] No literal colors, fonts, `!important` or `::ng-deep`.
- [ ] Files are in the right layer and segment; no deep imports into another slice.
- [ ] Loading, empty, no-results, error and success states exist and look right.
- [ ] Works at 390 px and with the keyboard; icon-only buttons have `ariaLabel`.
- [ ] Texts come from i18n keys or inputs.
- [ ] `npx eslint` on the changed files is clean; tests pass.

## Definition of done for a screen

1. It renders with the default theme and with a tenant theme, in light and dark mode.
2. It handles the five states.
3. It passes lint and its tests.
4. It has no console errors.

<!-- chapter 11: docs/manual/11-releases-and-contributing.md -->

# Releases and contributing

```bash
# One commit on main = one release
npm test && npm run build:showcase
git commit -m "feat(solercia): add sol-segmented-progress"
git tag v0.9.0
git push origin main && git push origin v0.9.0
```

Every commit that lands on `main` is a release and carries its own version tag. The tag triggers the
publish workflow; nobody publishes from a laptop.

## The release flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["Change + spec + showcase + docs"] --> B["Bump version<br/>and CHANGELOG"]
  B --> C["Commit to main"]
  C --> D["Tag vX.Y.Z"]
  D --> E["publish.yml<br/>tag = version?"]
  E -->|yes| F["npm publish<br/>Trusted Publishing + provenance"]
  E -->|no| G["Fails: fix the tag or the version"]
```

1. In the same commit, bump `version` in `projects/solercia/ui/package.json` and add the entry to
   `projects/solercia/ui/CHANGELOG.md`.
2. Commit, then tag the commit with exactly the library version: `git tag v<version>`.
3. Push the commit and the tag.
4. `.github/workflows/publish.yml` runs the tests, checks that the tag matches the version and publishes
   to npm only if that version is not published yet.

An untagged commit on `main` is a defect: tag it before anything else. A pushed tag is never moved or
deleted.

## Versioning

The packages follow [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/):

| Change | Bump |
| --- | --- |
| Fixes, documentation | `patch` |
| New components, inputs or outputs | `minor` |
| Removing or changing an exported symbol, selector, input or output | `major` |

While a package is below 1.0, a `minor` version may include breaking changes; the changelog says so
explicitly. The changelog follows [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/).

## Trusted Publishing

The packages publish with npm Trusted Publishing (OIDC): there is no npm token in the repository or
its secrets, and every version carries a provenance statement linking it to the commit and workflow
that built it. The Trusted Publisher configured on npmjs.com is organization `solercia-solutions`, the
package's repository and workflow `publish.yml`; an `ENEEDAUTH` error means one of the three does not
match.

## Contributing a change to `@solercia/ui`

```bash
npm ci
npm start              # showcase on http://localhost:4200
npm test               # library + schematics build, then Vitest (zoneless)
npm run build:showcase # must pass: CI builds it
```

A new or changed public component needs, in the same change:

- [ ] A spec covering its states, keyboard use and accessible names.
- [ ] A page or variant in `projects/showcase`.
- [ ] Its entry in the README (overview table and reference) and in `llms.txt`.
- [ ] The relevant chapter of this manual updated, and `npm run docs:llms` run to regenerate
      `llms-full.txt` (CI fails when it is out of date).
- [ ] New `shared.*` texts in both `i18n/en.json` and `i18n/es-CO.json`.

Code rules: standalone, `OnPush`, signal inputs and outputs, no zone.js; styles only through
`var(--sol-*)`; visible texts through `SOL_I18N` keys or inputs. In specs, create helper templates
before the component under test.

## Commit messages

Conventional Commits with scope `solercia`, a header of at most 72 characters in lowercase, and a body
of two to four bullets of at most 100 characters. Commits carry no tool or AI attribution.

```text
fix(solercia): confirm dialog as a bottom sheet on phones

- opens full width below 640 px with stacked actions and cancel at the bottom
- every action reaches the 44 px touch target on touch screens
```

## Documentation outputs

| Command | Produces |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run docs:site` | The *Guides* pages of the showcase in `projects/showcase/public/docs-content/` (run by `npm start` and `npm run build:showcase`) |
| `npm run docs:llms` | `llms-full.txt` at the repository root; `npm run docs:llms:check` fails when it is stale |
| `npm run docs:manual` | `dist/manual/solercia-design-system.pdf` and `.docx` (local tool; needs Pandoc and a local Chromium) |

<!-- chapter 12: docs/manual/12-faq.md -->

# FAQ

```ts
// The smallest working setup: one provider, the bundled theme, English texts.
import { ApplicationConfig } from '@angular/core';
import { provideTheme } from '@solercia/ui';

export const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = { providers: [provideTheme()] };
```

## Adoption

**Do I need all three packages?**
No. `@solercia/ui` is the only required one. `ng add` installs `@solercia/eslint-config`;
`@solercia/chat` is for applications that embed an assistant.

**Does it need zone.js?**
No. The library and the showcase run with `provideZonelessChangeDetection()`, the Angular 22 default.

**Can I adopt it screen by screen in an existing application?**
Yes. Register `provideTheme()`, add the tokens base to `styles.css` and use components in the screens
you touch. See [Getting started](https://github.com/solercia-solutions/solercia-ui/blob/main/docs/manual/03-getting-started.md#b-existing-project).

**Which Angular versions are supported?**
Angular 22 (`^22.0.0` peer dependencies).

## Theming

**Where do tenant themes come from?**
From your `THEME_SOURCE` implementation: an API, a static file, a database column. The library never
fetches a theme itself.

**What happens if a tenant theme is broken?**
`ThemeService` validates every document. An invalid theme, a failed request or a 404 keeps the default
theme and logs a console warning; the application never renders unstyled.

**Is dark mode part of the tenant theme?**
Each theme defines both modes, but which mode is active is the user's preference, stored in
`localStorage` and toggled with `ThemeService.toggleMode()`.

**Can I use my own colors in a component?**
Use the `--sol-*` tokens. If no token fits, the theme is missing a decision: add it to the theme, not to
the component.

## Texts and languages

**Why does a component show a key such as `pages.projects.empty.title`?**
The key is missing from your catalog: inputs ending in `Key` receive keys, and an engine returns the
key itself when it does not know it. Add the key to your translations.

**How do I get Spanish texts?**
`{ provide: SOL_I18N, useFactory: () => createSolI18n({ lang: 'es-CO' }) }`, or merge
`@solercia/ui/i18n/es-CO.json` into your engine's `es-CO` catalog.

## Extending

**The component I need does not exist. What now?**
Compose existing components in your application's `shared/ui` or feature first. If the need is
general, propose it to the library with a use case; it will get a spec, a showcase page and docs.

**Can I override a component's internal styles?**
No `::ng-deep` and no `!important`. Customize through inputs and the theme tokens a component reads.

**Can I use Chart.js or the CDK directly?**
Not in application code: the lint preset restricts them to the wrappers (`sol-chart`, `sol-kanban-*`)
so charts and drag and drop stay themed and accessible.

## Documentation

**Where is the complete list of inputs and outputs?**
In the [component reference](https://github.com/solercia-solutions/solercia-ui/blob/main/README.md#component-reference) of the README, and live in the
showcase.

**How do I regenerate the PDF and Word manual?**
`npm run docs:manual`. It needs Pandoc and a local Chromium; see
[Releases and contributing](https://github.com/solercia-solutions/solercia-ui/blob/main/docs/manual/11-releases-and-contributing.md#documentation-outputs).

**What should an AI agent read?**
[`llms-full.txt`](https://github.com/solercia-solutions/solercia-ui/blob/main/llms-full.txt): every chapter and the component reference in one file. See
[For AI agents](https://github.com/solercia-solutions/solercia-ui/blob/main/docs/manual/10-for-ai-agents.md).

---

# Appendix: component reference

### Actions

#### `sol-button` — `SolButtonComponent`
Text button with variants, sizes and a loading state.

| Input | Type | Default | Req |
|---|---|---|---|
| `variant` | `'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'danger' \| 'ghost'` | `'primary'` | |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| 'touch'` | `'md'` | |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | |
| `type` | `string` | `'button'` | |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | |

Outputs: `clicked: void`. Content: label (`<ng-content>`).

```html
<sol-button variant="danger" size="sm" [loading]="saving()" (clicked)="remove()">Delete</sol-button>
```

#### `sol-icon-button` — `SolIconButtonComponent`
Icon-only button; `ariaLabel` is mandatory.

| Input | Type | Default | Req |
|---|---|---|---|
| `icon` | `SolIconName` | — | yes |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | — | yes |
| `type` | `'button' \| 'submit'` | `'button'` | |
| `variant` | `'default' \| 'danger' \| 'ghost' \| 'outline'` | `'default'` | |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| 'touch'` | `'md'` | |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | |

Outputs: `clicked: void`.

```html
<sol-icon-button icon="trash" variant="danger" ariaLabel="Delete project" (clicked)="remove()" />
```

#### `sol-icon` — `SolIconComponent`
Inline SVG from the built-in registry (~140 names: `home`, `menu`, `edit`, `trash`, `calendar`, `bell`, `sun`, `moon`, …; full list in the showcase *Icon* page).

| Input | Type | Default | Req |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `SolIconName \| string` | — | yes |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | |
| `variant` | `'outline' \| 'fill'` | `'outline'` | |

```html
<sol-icon name="star" size="lg" variant="fill" />
```

```html
                 (fileSelected)="upload($event)" (fileError)="error.set($event)" />
```

Rich text editor (headings, lists, alignment, links, tables, images, @mentions, #task links); output HTML is TCPDF-safe.

| `linkableTasks` | `LinkableTask[]` (`{ key, title }`) | `[]` | |

Outputs: `valueChange: string`, `mentionsChange: string[]`, `taskLinksChange: string[]`.

```html

```
```ts
upload: SolRichImageUploader = (file) => this.api.uploadImage(file); // resolves the public URL
```
